statement: For every integer n≥1, all exact directed supports on n vertices requiring nSSP over the reals have at least 2n−1 arcs, and an exact support requiring nSSP with exactly 2n−1 arcs exists at the same n.

domain.matrices: All real n×n matrices; arbitrary nonzero weights and signs at the prescribed ordered pairs
domain.supports: Subsets of [n]×[n], loops allowed and counted once, no parallel multiplicity
domain.nssp: For every real X, A∘X=0 and AX^T=X^TA imply X=0; no extra diagonal or trace condition
domain.requires: Every realization of the exact support has nSSP
domain.allows: At least one realization of the exact support has nSSP
domain.positive_order_boundary: n=1 is attained by a single loop; n=0 is excluded

posing_source.title: Combinatorial aspects of the nonsymmetric strong spectral property for graphs
posing_source.locator: Problem 1.8, printed p. 759; Definitions 1.1 and 1.3, pp. 755–756
posing_source.exact_question: Is the minimum number of arcs in a directed graph G on n vertices that requires the nSSP equal to 2n−1?
posing_source.upper_construction_locator: Theorem 5.5, p. 771, with m=1; Remark 2.10(A), p. 764

proof_map.method: Cyclic decomposition over R[t] and multiplication on cyclic factors
F↦(a_ij f_ji); nSSP gives injectivity and diagonal commutation gives zero boundary

proof_map.claim: A requiring support is weakly connected
proof_map.method: Loopless component diagonal obstruction; looped supports sharing eigenvalue 1; off-block rank-one obstruction

proof_map.claim: Endpoint-looped bidirected paths require nSSP at every positive order
proof_map.method: Odd-offset propagation, first-column vanishing and a cyclic endpoint vector

written_corollaries: For any nSSP matrix with c weak support components, m≥2n−c.
Any weakly connected support allowing nSSP has m≥2n−1.
Both questions of Koljančić–Oblak Problem 2.9, printed p. 764, have minimum 2n−1.
No sign pattern on a weakly connected support with at most 2n−2 nonzero positions allows nSSP.
For a connected nSSP matrix with m=2n−1, dim Z(A)=n and the support readout is an isomorphism onto ker B.
